facts.text: Falcon Descent Stage was deployed at Hadley Rille during Apollo 15 in 1971.
Lower half of Lunar Module Falcon. Apollo 15 was the first 'J-mission' — a longer stay with more science, a rover, and three EVAs totalling over 18 hours outside.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Served as the base for the first extended lunar surface stay (66.9 hours), validating systems for prolonged human operations in the deep-space environment.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Hadley Rille.
Remains at Hadley-Apennine; its ascent stage was deliberately crashed into the Moon 93 km from the ALSEP, creating a calibrated seismic source.
